name: en_chinmaya_day06
transcript: Om Om Sahana bhavatu. Sahano bhunaktu. Sahaviryam karavavahe. Te Om Shanti Om Shanti Shanti Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra Marutah stunvanti divyai stavaih vedai sangapadakramopanishadaih gayanti yam samagaha Dhyanavasthita tadgatena manasa pashyanti yam yoginah yasyantam na vidussuraasuraganah devaya tasmai namah devaya tasmai namah Tasmai. Seeing Arjuna grieving. and also seeking the right understanding, a solution to completely eradicate his delusion. Bhagwan starts his discourse by giving the knowledge of the self. So Bhagwan says, Arjuna, if you had only known the nature of your true self, you would not be grieving like this. Grief is a sign of ignorance. Grief is a sign of ignorance of the self. So what is this self? So Bhagwan goes on to describe the nature of this self. The supreme self, which is of the nature of Sachit Anand, it is Nitya eternal. Then, Sat Swaroopaha, the only thing which is real. Everything else borrows its existence from this Sat Swaroopa. Also it is sarvagataha, all pervading. This self is aprameyah, which cannot be known as the object, but it is a very subject in us. It is akarta, non-doer. Abhokta, non-enjoyer, and Nirvikara Swarupa. Freedom from any kind of modifications. This is the nature of the self. This one must understand and only then such a person can live a life of happiness and peace. So Arjuna, as far as your grief is concerned, there is no need to grieve because, as far as the self is concerned, it is imperishable. As far as the Jivatma is concerned, again Jivatma is also imperishable. The body dies but the Jivatma which is nothing but the Sukshma Sharira. It goes from body to body. Just like a person drops the cloth, the old worn out cloth and takes up the new cloth, in the same way the Jivatma also takes up, takes up the new body and continues his existence. So therefore there is no non-existence for Jivatma. As far as the body is concerned, anyway it is inert. It has come from the element, it will go back to the element. Again it will come back again from these elements. So even if you consider an individual to be merely the body, what is there to grieve? The body has come from the elements. During death, it goes back to the element. Again from these elements, again a new body is born. So even with respect to the body also, there is no need to grieve. Now, from the standpoint of Dharma, Bhagwan analyzes the situation. Bhagwan says, Arjuna, there is no need to grieve from the standpoint of Dharma also. There is actually, there is no need to get confused because everything is so clear. So what is Bhagwan's argument? Let us chant verse number 31, 32. Svadharmamapi cha veksha navikampitumarhasi. Dharmadhiyuddhatsheyonyat kshatriyasya na vidyate. Yadruchchayachopappannam. Swargadvaramapavritam sukhinakshatriyah partha labhante yuddhamidrusham Svadharmam apicha apekshya. Arjuna, even if we consider this situation from the standpoint of your swadharma, your duty, navikampitum arhasi, there is no need to waver. There is no need to get confused. Even from the standpoint of your swadharma, I don't see any reason why you should get confused because Dharmayuddha shreyah anyat kshatriyasya na vidyate. As far as a Kshatriya is concerned, the greatest shreyas, the ultimate good that can happen to a Kshatriya is he waging the war of a dharma yuddha. As far as a Kshatriya is concerned, the best thing that can happen is to get a chance to wage a war which is righteous. So Arjuna, as far as your case is concerned, you are waging a righteous war. So what is the need of wavering? What Bhagwan is trying to say is, sometimes what happens is a soldier is forced to fight an unrighteous war because a soldier has to just obey the orders of his superiors. So very many times it may so happen that a soldier has to Wage an unrighteous war, so there is a conscience prick in him which will, that conscience prick is called vikampanam. Somewhere deep within you are not justifying your own act. Somewhere deep within you know that the rival is right and I am wrong. In such a case, when a soldier has to fight the war, it becomes a little difficult. The conscience doesn't allow him to do, but at the same time, his duty says he has to obey the orders of the superiors. Arjuna, as far as you are concerned, that case is also not there. Because in your case, even the rivals know that they are on the unrighteous path. Bhishma, Drona, Kripacharya, all of them know that Pandavas are right and Kauravas are wrong. So as far as you are concerned, you are waging a righteous war, there is no need for any conscience break also. Also, Arjuna, as far as this war is concerned, how has it come to you? Yadruchchaya cha upapannam. It has come to you upapannam. How? Yadruchchaya. Yadruchchaya means by itself, without being sought. on its own accord. It has come by itself Arjuna. You have not asked for it. It has come by itself to you. So such a war is considered to be Swargadvaram Apavritam. Apavritam Swargadvaram. Apavritam means Wide open. What is wide open? Dwaram, the gates. Gates of what? Swargam. Swarga Dwaram Apavritam. Arjuna, as far as this war is concerned, it is an entry to the Swarga with its gates wide open for you. Meaning even if you die in the war straight you will go to Swarga alone. So therefore what is the need for grieving? Arjuna Sukhina Kshatriyah Partha labhante yuddhamidrusham. Those soldiers, those warriors who get such a wonderful opportunity, they are indeed blessed ones, they are indeed the most fortunate ones. Number one, they are asked to perform their duty. Number two, they have to wage a righteous war. Number three, they have not asked for itself, it has come by its own accord. These conditions are very rare to fulfill. And in your case, these conditions are fulfilled. So therefore, Arjuna, you must consider yourself to be the most blessed. for having asked to fight a war which is righteous and which has come on its own accord. So therefore, when you do this swadharma, you are not doing any kind of papa, you are only performing punya karma. But suppose Arjuna you step back deciding not to fight, then what will happen next verse. Athachetvamimam dharmayam sangramam nakarishyasi. Tatasva dharmam kirtim cha hitva papamavapsyasi. Ath, athachet. In case. Imam, tvam imam dharmiyam sangramam na karishyasi. In case if you don't fight this war, this righteous war, If you don't fight, then tataha swadharma keertim chahitva papam avapsyasi. Then you will not be performing your swadharma also. Kirtim cha hitva, because you don't perform your duty, you will only bring ill fame and disgrace to yourself. And this way, papam avapsasi, you will only attain papam. Not performing your duty, you will attain only Papa. So when do we get Papa? When what is called as Papa? Papa is that what you are supposed to do you are not doing or you do what you are not supposed to do. Both are papa only. When you do what you are not supposed to do, or when you don't do what you are supposed to do, both are papa. So in this case, Arjuna, you are supposed to fight this war. And you are not fighting it, it will only amount to Papa. So therefore, it will not take you to Swarga. Also in this very life itself, you will only bring ill fame to yourself, disgrace to yourself. So now here Bhagwan is clearly Making Arjuna understand the pros and cons. If you fight the war, what you will get? If you don't fight, what you will get? In fact, if you don't fight, what you will lose rather. So this is from the dharmic standpoint, from the moral standpoint. Arjuna, you must perform your duty. Now from the worldly standpoint. Let us chant 34, 35, 36. Akeertim chapi bhutani kathayishyanti tevyayam. Sambhavitasya cha kirtih maranadatirichyate bhayadranaduparatam matsyante tvam maharathah Yesham chatvam bahumatah bhutvayasyasi laghavam avachyavadascha bahun vadishyanti tavahitah Nindantastava samarthyam tato duhkhataram nu kim. Yes. Now from the worldly standpoint, absolutely worldly laukika drishti. What does Bhagwan say? Arjuna, do you know what will happen if you don't fight the war? Suppose you withdraw, then what will happen? What will be the consequences you will have to face? Akirtim chapi bhutani kathaishanti te avyayam. All these bhutani, all the people, they will not praise you. for your peaceful initiatives, that you did not fight the war. Because of the bad consequences of the war, you stepped back, all the people will not praise you, instant avyayam constantly. All through your life and all through ages and generations, what will they do? Kathaishyansi. They will keep on describing, discussing what? Akeertin. Your disgrace, your ill fame. That act of disgrace, that will be the constant topic of discussion among all people. Books will be written. TV programs will happen. In the news channel, again and again, this will come. Just imagine. And what is the topic of discussion? How this person is wrong? How he has brought ill fame to himself. This will be the topic of discussion and it's a fact. You see, 5000 years have passed, even now what are we discussing? That despondency of Arjuna. Only once he had that state, even today we are discussing that, isn't it? Ages after ages, this discussion will continue. So Arjuna, avyayam, constantly, this will be the topic of discussion. People are interested in all negative things only. A person has done 1000 good things, it will not be there in the newspaper. He has fallen once, that will be the main headline. This is the nature of people. Are you aware of this? One small step from your side has got such long lasting consequences. Are you aware of it? For a person, sambhavitasya cha akirtihi maranat atirichyate. Now what will happen to you? Who are you? Sambhavitaha, the one who has earned name, fame, respect, reverence from everyone including the rivals, the enemies. They all respect you, revere you. You are a man of great reputation in the society. For such a person, akirti when ill fame comes, when dishonor comes, disgrace come for such a person, maranat atirichyate for him, this disgrace is Even worse than death. Death is far better. You're not an ordinary person, you're a man of reputation. For a man of reputation, Disgraces even worse than death also. And as far as your rivals are concerned, do you know what they will say suppose you step back? Bhayat ranat uparatam matsyante tvam maharathaha. All those maharathis who are standing in the other side. your rivals, your enemies. As far as you are concerned, yesham chatvam bahumataha, they have great respect for you. No doubt you are the enemy. Even to the enemy like you, they have great respect for you. Even the enemies have great respect for you. Because you are such a valorous person. You are a game changer and therefore that respect is there. What will happen suppose you step back? Bhootva yasyaasi laghavam, you will become small in their eyes. Now you are a big personality in their eyes, if you step back, you will become small. And do you know what they will say? Bhayad ranad uparatam. He has run away out of fear, this is what they will say. Out of fear of Karna, because Karna was the main rival of Arjuna. He knew that he would lose the battle against Karna, therefore he ran away from there. in the name of peace. Darbok, a coward, he ran away from war. This is what they will say. They will not appreciate your thoughts of peace and this and that, no way. They will say you ran away from the battlefield out of fear. And then avachya vadaancha bahoon vadishyanti tava ahitaha. All your ahitas, people who want bad things to happen to you, your enemies, what will they say? They will speak such unspeakable words. Now what is that unspeakable words? You have to just imagine. Swamiji, what is it? The very fact that it is unspeakable means I should not also should not speak. Unparliamentary words will be used against you. Avachyavadan. Nindantastava samarthyam, your might, your strength, they will make fun of. They will ridicule your might, your strength. Tato duhkhataram nu kim? What can be a cause of greater sorrow than that? Have you ever imagined what will happen? Now this is from the laukika drishti, from the very worldly standpoint. Very many times what happens is ordinary people understand only this worldly standpoint. They will not understand philosophical standpoint or moral standpoint, they will not understand. Adhyatmika drishti they will not understand. Dharmika drishti they will not understand, they will understand this one, laukika drishti. Very many people are doing good only because of this srishti. What will others think of me? What will others talk of me? So at least let me do something good. So Bhagwan is using that strategy also. Arjuna, forget about everything, philosophy, etcetera. Do you know what they will speak about you? You will not be even fit to live in the society. That will be your condition. So therefore Arjuna, listen to me. This situation is a win-win situation. How? Verse number 37. Hato va prapsyasi swargam jitva va bhokshyase mahim tasmaduttistha kaunteya yuddha Bhayakruta nishchayah. Arjuna, in both ways you are only going to gain. You are only going to benefit. What are the two ways? There are only two possibilities as far as you are concerned. Either hato hato va prapsyasi swargam. One possibility is you will die in this battlefield. Enemies will kill you. In that case, where will you go? Prapsyasi swargam, you will get swarga. Or the other possibilities, you will win the war. Then what will happen? Jitva va bhogshyase mahim. If you win, then you will enjoy this earth, the kingdom, the pleasures, everything. Power, position, everything you will enjoy. So these are the only two possibilities. Either you will die in the battlefield or you will win the battle. If you die in the battlefield, you will straight go to Swarga and enjoy all the pleasures there. If you win the battle, you will enjoy the pleasures here. So in both ways you are going to enjoy, isn't it? So it is a Win-win situation. What was Arjuna's analysis? It is a loose-loose situation. Now see that. The same thing, two different people viewing from two different perspectives with two different kinds of knowledge. When your understanding is not clear, you see how even a golden opportunity is seen as a crisis. Isn't it? When you have the right understanding, you see how even a crisis is seen as a golden opportunity. What makes the difference? The right understanding makes the difference. Situation is the same, two people analyzing the situation with different understanding. Bhagwan says Arjuna, you have only to gain, there is nothing to lose. Now here only two possibilities are given, there is a third possibility also. One is either he will die in the battlefield. The second is he will win the battle. There is a third possibility. What is the third possibility? He may lose the battle and be caught as a prisoner. That option also cannot be denied, isn't it? But then Bhagwan doesn't take that option. Why? Arjuna, as far as you are concerned, it's not possible. Because as long as you are alive, You cannot be defeated. That option itself is not discussed. Either you are alive and winning or you are dead. So therefore Arjuna, in any case, you are only going to benefit therefore. Tasmāt uttiṣṭha kaunteya, oh son of Kunti, get up. Yuddhāya kruta niścayaḥ. firmly determining to fight. So even from the laukika drishti also you must fight. From adhyatmika drishti you must fight, from dharmika drishti you must fight, from laukika drishti also you must fight. Where is the confusion? I don't see any confusion at all. But Arjuna, how you should fight, even while fighting. How to fight in such a way that your mind is not disturbed at all. I will tell you a technique. What is that technique? A very, very wonderful verse, very practical verse for everyone, irrespective of whether you are spiritual or not. Let us see that verse, verse number 38. Sukha duhkhe same krutva labhalabhau jaya jayau tato yuddhaya yujyasva naivam papamavapsyasi Yes, Arjuna, how you must fight, I will tell you. In this way if you fight, naivam papam avapsyasi. You will never attain papa, meaning your mind will not be disturbed. Disturbance of the mind itself is papa. What is sin? Disturbance of the mind is sin. Whenever you do sin, what happens to your mind? Disturbed. So, if your mind is disturbed, what does it mean? You are committing sin. Sin and disturbance, they go together. So Arjuna, there is a way in which you can fight without disturbing the mind. How? Why are you fighting? Let there be clarity. How you should fight? The fight should be taken up in such a way, sukha dukhe samekritva, consider sukha and dukha sama, same. Labha labhou jaya jayo, consider labha and alabha. Labha and nashta, same. Jaya ajaya, consider them to be same. Jaya, victory. Ajay, loss. Labha, gain. Nashta, loss. So victory, defeat, gain, loss, joy, sorrow, consider them to be equal and then fight. What does it mean? See, what is it that we want? What we want is not victory. What we want is not profit. What we want is peace of mind, isn't it? We are seeking victory for peace. We are seeking profit for peace. We are seeking everything for peace. Bhagwan says if this is what you are seeking, make it very clear to the mind that I want peace. Therefore, don't make choice with regard to the results of the future. If you say I want only this, there is a possibility that you may not get it and then your peace will be disturbed. So when you are saying I want only victory, what are you doing? You are having a raga towards victory and dwesha towards defeat. It is as though you have already chosen the future, the uncertain future. You have no idea what is going to be there in the future, but already you have made the choice. So what happens if you don't get what you wanted? If you don't get what you crave for, your mind will be disturbed. When you get attached to an uncertain future, what will be the state of your mind? Disturbance. There will be anxiety, there will be worry, there will be fear. Will I get what I want or not? Will I get what I want or not? The best thing is don't want anything. Instead of worrying about some uncertain future, instead of wanting something, drop that want. Because it is this want that creates disturbance. A great psychology. Don't want, want peace. And for that peace, you don't have to wait for the future. Right now, you can be peaceful. As far as peace is concerned, you don't have to wait for the future. Right in this moment, you can be peaceful. Make that decision that I want peace. How to practice it? Don't allow the mind to go to the future. Don't allow the mind to go to the past. In the past, you will have only regrets. Drop the regrets of the past. And the anxieties of the future remain in the present. Drop the excitement of the present also. Excitement is connected to the results of the future. Remain in the present. Now, in the present, how you should occupy your mind because mind wants something. Mind cannot remain idle. So what has, what you should do with your mind? Now the mind cannot escape into the future or the past, it has to remain in the present, but it should be occupied. So what you should do? Yuddhaya yujyasva. Pay attention to what you are doing in the present. Remain consciously aware of what you are doing in the present. Bring the mind there. Bring the mind in the here and now. Remain in the present moment. You practice this and you will find the mind is peaceful. A very practical technique. In fact, this is one of the techniques practiced by these Zen masters. In all these stories you will find this. What disciple asked, I mean, some seeker asked a disciple of a great master, what do your master do? He's a realized master, what does he do? Then this disciple said, he eats when he eats. He sleeps when he sleeps. Over. You understood. The point is, very many times we do something, but our mind is not there. The mind is somewhere wandering. Thinking about something, planning something, imagining something, worrying about something. Where is the mind? Except where your hands are, isn't it? This is called conscious living or sometimes it is called mindful living. This is something which all of us can practice. What is the practice? Whatever little little things you do in life, it may be getting up from the bed. brushing your teeth. Even that can be meditative, you know. It can be a meditation. Taking bath. What you have to do is just bring the mind to what you are doing. Your hands are lifting. The hand lifts, lifting the water mug and you're pouring. Pay attention to that. Your hand being lifted. The water droplets trickling down your body, feel it, feel it. Make the action very, very slow so that you can pay attention to the minute details of what is happening in you. This is called conscious living. You are conscious of everything what is happening. So then what happens? The mind is occupied in the present. Mind is not idle. You have given a task to the mind and what is the task? Pay attention to the present moment, to the present activity. Along with if you can make your breath very slow and steady. And now and then you can pay attention to your breath also, then you will find that steady slow breath starts contributing to the peace of your mind. Because slow steady breathing naturally has to lead to a peaceful mind. So this is a practice now. You will find that when you start practicing this even the jobs which are most boring. That boredom will go away. It may be mopping the floor. It may be washing the dishes. It may be washing your clothes. Just pay attention to your hands. Pay attention to your bodily movements. Do it slowly. At the same time, breathing slowly, steadily. Now the mind is not thinking of anything. Whenever the mind thinks of something, immediately bring it to the present. You will find that 5, 10 minutes you practice it, your mind has become steady. Why? To a great extent, when the mind is in the present, it has nothing to do. Now the mind is not worrying, the mind is not tensed, mind is on imagining. Mind is not imagining, mind is not planning, and the number of thoughts needed to remain in the present is minimum, what happens to the mind? It becomes helplessly quiet. Just practice it and see. Whatever you do, slow the whole speed. If you brush for say 5 minutes, make it 10 minutes. Slowly do everything and feel everything what happens inside the mouth when you are rubbing your brush against your teeth, feel it. Feel the movement of your hands. Feel the movement of your fingers, the wrist, the palm. Feel that feeling inside the teeth, the mouth, everything. And then you will find the mind has become peaceful. On one side action is continuously happening, on the other side your mind is taking deep rest. Then you, this itself is yoga actually. Very many people think meditation means sit, giving up all your work in a secluded place. Good, that also should be done. But throughout the day, you can't do that. You will have to enter into your professional fields. Work is necessary. Then how to do this work? This is the way. Very, very practical technique and something which everyone can do, even a child can do this. Pujya Gurudev used to say, bring your mind where your hands are. Most of the energies are dissipated and drained in us only because the mind is thinking of the future. The worries, anxieties, 99% of the energy is not exhausted because of the bodily work. It is because of the Mental leakage. And the mental leakage happens through the future or through the past. Either the person is thinking all the negativities of the past. Or the person is thinking, planning about the future. I cannot say planning, I have to say worrying about the future. Planning is good, worrying is bad. When you plan, you consciously think, that is called planning. When you worry, you unconsciously worry. Whichever is conscious effort, energy is less. Whichever is unconscious, energy is more. Energy wasted is more. So it is a very practical means. What you have to do? Remain in the present. This is the meaning. Arjuna, sukha dukhe samay krutva. As far as your situation is concerned, outer environment is concerned, either it can be sukha or dukha, don't be judgmental. Because for that, mind has to do a lot of unnecessary work. You are in this situation, You are in a choiceless situation, accept the situation and do what is necessary for that situation. Sukha dukhe samai krutva means what? Stop worrying about sukha or dukha, whether this situation is sukha or dukha, stop it. It is not necessary. Stop the mental leakage, judging the situation, comparing the situation, commenting about the situation. Not necessary. As far as the future is concerned, labha alabhau, jaya ajayau. Will I win or not? This is Jaya Ajaya. What will I gain? What will I lose? This is Labha Alabha. Stop. Put a full stop. With respect to them, give up your raga dwesha, likes and dislikes. You want peace, isn't it? Peace is available in this moment. Right now, you can be peaceful. What you have to do? Bring the mind to the present. And in the present, what is your job? Yuddhaya yujyasva. Your job is to fight, pay attention to your duty, full stop. In this case if you live, nainam papam avapsyasi. You will find your mind is not disturbed at all. There is no reason why the mind should be disturbed. The mind will be at peace. This way Arjuna fight the war. Now this topic is over here. Now Bhagwan starts up the next topic. Let us chant the verse first. Yesha tebhihita sankhye Buddhir Yogetvimam Shrano Buddhya Yukto Yaya Partha Karma Bandham Prahasyasi. Yes, Arjuna, till now. I have given you Abhihita, I have explained to you Sankhye Buddhihi. Here Buddhihi means knowledge. Till now what have I given you? I have given the knowledge of Sankhya. What do you mean Sankhya? Atma, self. We have seen this. Sam plus kya. Kya means to know. So what is Sankhya? Brahmavidya is called Sankhya, the knowledge of the Upanishad. So what is Sankhya? That which is in Sankhya. which is described in Sankhya. So what is it? Atma, the supreme self. So now Bhagwan says Arjuna, till now I have given you the knowledge about the supreme self. This was the discussion mainly. Not that Swadharma this that etcetera. Especially from 12 to 25 these verses they are mainly related to. the self knowledge. Till now I have given you that. Now I am going to give you something else Arjuna. What is that? Yogi tu imam shrunu. Now listen to yoga buddhi. Till now you have listened to Sankhya buddhi, now listen to yoga buddhi. Sankhya Buddhi means the knowledge of the self. Yoga Buddhi means how to prepare oneself for that knowledge, in short, Karma Yoga. In simple sentence, Arjuna, till now I have given you Gnana Yoga. Now I will give you Karma Yoga. Bhagwan, why do you want to give me this? Buddhyayukto yaya partha, with this buddhi, with this knowledge, karma bandham prahasayasi. You will be free from karma bandhana, bondage of action. You will be free from karma bandhana. Meaning you will be free from samsara. You will be free from birth death cycle. Arjuna, till now I have given you the knowledge of the self. Now I am going to give you how to prepare your mind so that you can gain this knowledge. Both are necessary. Self-knowledge cannot be gained through an unprepared mind. With an unprepared mind, even if a person is exposed to the self-knowledge, nothing will happen. So what has to be done? The vessel has to be prepared. It is through the mind we have to gain the knowledge, but the mind has to be prepared. So how to prepare the mind? That is the very essence of Yoga Buddhi. That is the very essence of Karma Yoga. Arjuna, now I will give you that. So that you can prepare the mind first, and with that such a prepared mind, you can gain this knowledge, and after gaining this knowledge, Karma bandham prahasya si. You can be free from the bondage of action. So both are necessary. What are the two stages? First stage, preparation of the mind, second stage, gaining the knowledge. Prepare the mind. Gain the knowledge through such a prepared mind and then with that knowledge become free. This is the logic. So Arjuna, now I am going to give you this. Arjuna, this yoga buddhi, this karma yoga is an excellent thing. Now Bhagwan is praising this karma yoga. Bhagwan is a very good advertiser of his product. So what is the greatness of Karma Yoga? Let us see verse number 40. Neha Vikrama Nashosti Pratyavayo na vidyate. Svalpamapyasya dharmasya trayate mahato bhaya. Yes. Arjuna, this karma yoga is unique. It is very unique. It has no drawbacks. Anyone can practice it. Anyone can practice it. Actually, it is very easy. As far as action is concerned, if you want to be successful, what are the factors necessary? So first of all, let us see the meaning of this. Na iha abhikramanashah asti. In this karma yoga, iha means in this karma yoga, abhikramanasha is not there. Abhikrama means beginning. Abhikrama also means undertaking. So there is no loss of beginning or there is no loss of undertaking. Pratyavayaha na vidyate. There is no pratyavaya also. Pratyavaya means adverse effect, side effects. Swalpamapyasya dharmasya trayate mahato bhayat. Swalpam, even little if you practice this dharma, this path. Svalpamapi asya dharmasya if you practice trayate mahato bhayat you will be saved from great danger. Even a little bit of practice, you will be saved from a great danger. Now, let us spend some time here. As far as an ordinary action is concerned, any action in this world, not karma yoga, any action. If you want to succeed, what are necessary? What are the factors necessary? Number one, right effort has to be put. Every job demands a certain quota of efforts you have to put in. If a student has to pass, can pass an exam, there is an amount of effort. If the business has to succeed, there is an effort. So everywhere if you want to succeed, number one, right effort is needed. Number two, effort should be put in right sequence. Sequence is also important. Like for example, When the clothes become dirty, what is the first thing you do? You wash it. What is the second thing you do? You dry it. What is the third thing you do? You iron it. The sequence cannot be jumbled up. You can't first iron, then dry, then wash. That is not the way. So the second thing is right sequence. Krama. Abhikrama. Abhikrama also means undertaking. So right effort. Right effort, right sequence. Then right direction, right action must be performed.
